rubric_notes: All must_include met; correct SUNIDs for families, superfamily, fold, class, and a.4.5 (46785); a.4.5 relatives (forkhead, LexA, CAP) and H-NS a.155.1 supported by bundle. Superfamily vs fold vs class semantics correct; SOS, histone-modifier, and 'histone-like' transfer explicitly rejected. Minor: the claim that 2.08 is the API's current release is not backed by a /releases/current entry in this bundle, but it is a peripheral, non-fabricated statement and does not affect the classification evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

All identifiers (113676, 122676, 116993, 140797, 101386, 101385, A:7-93) correct. Note the cited resolve endpoints for a.204.1.2/a.204.1.4 return species nodes, so family SUNIDs and the hypothetical-protein label are not directly in the bundle, but the values are correct SCOPe 2.08 facts, not fabrications. Reasoning complete: superfamily homology, family divergence, explicit rejection of HisE/MazG function transfer, external evidence named.

Correct families with SUNIDs under c.55.1 (53067), fold c.55, class c, supported by children/parents/resolve endpoints. Infers remote common ancestry of an ancestral nucleotide-associated scaffold; distinguishes from fold/class-only similarity. Rejects transfer of substrate specificity, EC annotation, cellular role, kinetics, and notes a single representative cannot capture the functional diversity. Names required external evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

All identifiers (47241, 47253, 100951, 47240, 47239, 46456) correct for release 2.08. Interprets shared superfamily as probable common ancestry stronger than fold sharing, with conserved helical bundle as framework and changes in ligands, access channels, and assembly driving divergence; distinguishes fold and class semantics. States different chemistry does not disprove homology and that ancestry does not license transfer of iron storage, RNR, catalase activity, metal identity, or substrate specificity; requires sequence/ligand-residue comparison, experimental metal/cofactor identity, biochemical and oligomeric/partner evidence. Notes RNR-like family name does not imply RNR chemistry for all members. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families, superfamily, fold, class with SUNIDs matching bundle. Clear family-vs-superfamily-vs-fold semantics. Cites 'probably related to cupredoxins but lacking the metal-binding site' annotations (in bundle). Adds supported context: PAD4 catalytic C-terminal domain separately classified, and ephrin ectodomain (b.6.1.5) distinct from Eph receptor ligand-binding domain (b.18.1.4, in search results). Explicit evidence requirements for copper binding and redox function. No violations.

Correct family SCCS/SUNIDs under d.15.1 (54236), fold d.15 (54235), class d, release 2.08; bundle superfamily children confirm. Distinguishes superfamily homology from fold membership and notes family does not guarantee identical function. Explicitly rejects indiscriminate transfer of conjugation, degradation tagging, p97 binding, and Ras binding; notes not every ubiquitin-related protein is conjugatable and RBD is not a GTPase; names required evidence. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct superfamily c.23.1 (52172), families with SUNIDs, fold c.23 (52171), class c (51349); search results in bundle confirm family nodes 52173, 52252, 82344. Explicitly states the classification does not establish that the ancestor was an active response regulator, directly meeting must_avoid. Rejects Asp phosphorylation, kinase partners, DNA binding, chemotaxis, decarboxylation/PLP, and KaiA kinase/circadian attribution; frames relationships as domain-level. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

All identifiers correct and bundle-supported (51229, 310577, 310616; siblings b.84.1-b.84.4; fold comment). Family membership of V1 and A1 bulge domains supported by search results. Positive claim within b.84.5, only fold similarity across superfamilies, separation neither proves independent origin nor excludes deeper relationship; notes homology endpoint confirms the distinction; rejects function transfer and domain-to-subunit extrapolation. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Identifiers and hierarchy correct; correct central inference and limits; evidence requirements given as sequence/profile and detailed structural for homology, biochemical/complex-context for function. Does not draw on the f.21.3 possible-link annotation or superfamily comments, so the uncertainty discussion omits an alternative explanation SCOPe itself records. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct SCCS and SUNIDs for all three families, superfamily, fold, class; homology endpoint claim (homology_scope sf) supported by bundle. Clear divergent-evolution interpretation, refuses transfer of ADH activity, CoA binding, NAD(P) binding, gating mechanism; domain vs whole-protein distinction; required evidence types listed. No material errors.

Correct family SUNID 100905 with the 'not a true family' annotation, superfamily/fold/class supported by the bundle's parents call, states the level-based default does not override the specific annotation, describes the placements as a designed structural grouping that does not establish homology, contrasts with normal family/superfamily semantics, and refuses function/amyloidogenicity transfer. No unmet criteria. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Biological content complete: separate fold c.137 in 1.69 vs c.23.14.1; 2.08 c.23.14.2 and c.23.14.1 in shared superfamily c.23.14; correctly interprets as probable common ancestry stronger than fold resemblance, without family merge; function-transfer caveat given; uses d1t1ja1 as current SID. However the evidence bundle contains only resolve calls on SCCS strings (returning species nodes); the SID change d1t1ja_ to d1t1ja1, residue range 1-118, and SUNIDs 106249/31395 are asserted without cited API support. Claims are correct but the identifier change, a scoring focus, is unsupported by the answer's own evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Complete and correct: tag H:1-8 sunid 343393 l.1.1.1 Tags/Artifacts described as bookkeeping categories; biological d1a14h1 H:9-111 sunid 20061 VH b.1.1.1 with full hierarchy; tag similarity not natural homology evidence, could be shared engineered sequence or chance, exclude from homology/function/template inference; family/superfamily vs fold/class distinction and antigen-specificity caveat stated. Resolve responses support SIDs, SUNIDs, SCCS, and boundaries; level names are correct SCOPe 2.08 facts. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Accurate release history supported by its bundle: whole-chain d1acca_ f.11.1.1 through 2.03, split shown in 2.04 and retained through 2.06, 2.07, and 2.08, with correct SIDs, SUNIDs, boundaries, and hierarchy including the class b move for the PA14 unit. Reasoning covers modular evolutionary units, rejects fold-alone homology, refuses whole-chain and toxin-function transfer from a PA14 match, limits template use to the matched region, and calls for remapping legacy identifiers. Does not mention that the C-terminal unit still comprises three structural domains, leaving out the caveat that classified units need not match every structural subdivision.

All five SIDs, boundaries, and classifications correct and supported, including fold SUNID 345891; mosaic of reused modules vs new fold stated; caveats on ancestry, function transfer, and new-fold meaning present. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Strongest form of the required reasoning: shared family a.298.1.1, lengths reflect repeat number and construct extent rather than family-defining identity, and the 'single repeat' comment plus 're' flags on two domains plus the canonical representative repeat supply the annotation basis against inferring separate ancestry. Notes constructs are not full-length proteins and that length/34 does not yield repeat counts. Domain SUNIDs 264989/265556/265996, family SUNID 267609, hierarchy, and representative coordinate scope are all supported.

Reports 2.08 / 2.08-stable, release date, and periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16, supported by its /releases/current bundle. Citation guidance correct and rejects 'current'/'latest' alone. States the periodic label is a dated incremental update incorporating ongoing classification additions, not a new stable release and not a wholesale revision of the hierarchy, which captures the add-without-rewrite semantics. Freeze date omitted but not required. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All must_include points covered: shared a.47.2.1 placement with full SID list, fragment/ms annotations vs four-long-helix STAT-like fold, full-domain evidence recontextualizes fragments; recommends complete validated domain for fold interpretation and using fragments only for covered regions. Correct level semantics and function-transfer limits. 1dn1 obsolete/3c98 is a true external fact. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Rejects single-ancestor premise, explains convergent recruitment and divergence within superfamilies, caveats on classification limits, adds useful domain-level point for multidomain enzymes. Correct level semantics. Integrates sequence/profile beyond motif, topology and residue correspondence, distinctive shared features, phylogeny, biochemistry; rejects function/template transfer. c.2 (51734)/c.2.1 (51735) and c.3 (51904)/c.3.1 (51905) verified via sccs and children endpoints; homology warning for c.2 in bundle. 'Current API release' not backed by a /releases/current call but all endpoints return 2.08, so not material.

Accurate 2.04 versus 2.08 placements with SUNIDs, correct superfamily-level ancestry inference, explicit rejection of fold-only homology, use of the calcium-free N-terminal strand caveat against the calcium-bound 1nqd, the PubMed 17977833 family comment with the correct caution that it does not name 1dlc, and clean refusal of catalysis, specificity, and galactose-binding transfer. Attributes the current release and the periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16 to the API, but no release endpoint response is present in its evidence bundle to support that release-identification claim.

Homology upheld via family a.4.1.1 (46690) and Engrailed node; hf correctly defined, qualifies structural equivalence without negating homology, does not identify exemplar; interchangeable coordinates, contact geometry, DNA-binding specificity rejected; datasets retain hf, separate ancestry labels from structural targets, avoid pooling as equivalent fold examples, keep relatives together in splits. SUNIDs and comments supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Meets must_include: family member retained; fr coverage caveat with aligned-length/coverage reporting; d1uc6a1 preferred conditional on completeness/quality, fragment kept as labeled partial example. Diversity sampling and function-transfer limits stated. Identifiers and boundaries correct. Representative selection lacks any quality values or method/resolution. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct recommendation (new superfamily, provisional pending detailed comparison); family asserts probable ancestry plus distinct closer group; new fold requires distinct arrangement/connectivity and is not justified by failure to detect homology; explicit that absence of sequence similarity cannot exclude homology and that classification is evidence-integrating and revisable. Rejects function transfer. No release-specific claims; no factual errors.

Correct family descriptions, SCCS and SUNIDs, superfamily 56112, fold 56111, class d, all supported by the resolve/children/parents bundle entries. Clearly separates family (closer), superfamily (remote homology), fold (architecture only) and class. Bilobal beta-rich N-lobe/helical C-lobe architecture and metal-assisted phosphoryl transfer given as shared chemistry with explicit limits on catalytic competence. Refuses transfer of protein target, antibiotic spectrum, lipid substrate, activation-loop/cyclin/autoinhibition regulation, and PI3K regulatory-subunit/membrane recruitment. Evidence list complete (sequence/profile, phylogeny, residue conservation, ligand-bound structures, biochemical specificity, full-length organization, partners, modification sites, localization, mutational and cellular evidence). No errors.
